rituals.title: THREE WORLDS, ONE FACT
rituals.goal: One fact can support more than one world.
rituals.steps:
1. Keep Event — Keep the event fixed.
2. Invent — Invent three models for why it happened.
3. Predict Different — Each model must predict a different thing you could observe next.
4. Earliest — Notice the earliest observation that would separate them.
5. Speak Plurals — Until that evidence arrives, speak in plurals: possibilities, not prophecy.
rituals.win: ✓ Possibilities plural. Prophecy cancelled.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Speak Plurals”; leave the forecast.
• On return, repeat “Predict Different”.
• “Earliest” — fear isn’t fate.
• What changed: “Keep Event” → “Speak Plurals”?
• I can use “Invent” while fear stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Keep Event → Invent → Predict Different → Earliest → Speak Plurals
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not multiply theories when an urgent practical response is already clear.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: ADD THE PREFIX
rituals.goal: Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.
rituals.steps:
1. Prefix Thought — Take the exact thought and place these words before it: ‘I am noticing my mind produce…’ Say the complete sentence once at ordinary speed.
2. Check Command — Notice what remains true and what loses command authority.
3. Resume Task — Carry on with the next chosen task while the sentence exists nearby.
rituals.win: ✓ Urgency lost its shortcut to the decision.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Resume Task”; slow the clock.
• Pulled back? Touch “Check Command”.
• “Check Command” puts facts above speed.
• Difference check: “Prefix Thought” → “Resume Task”.
• I can use “Check Command” without rushing.
rituals.formula_flow: Prefix Thought → Check Command → Resume Task
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Drop the wording if it feels mocking, unreal, or destabilising.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THANKS, MIND. NO CONTRACT.
rituals.goal: Protection can be acknowledged without being hired.
rituals.steps:
1. Ask Danger — Ask what danger the thought is trying to prevent.
2. Thank Intention — Offer a precise thank-you for that intention.
3. Answer M — Then answer: ‘I’m not signing this instruction.’ Choose a matching what matters to you action that keeps any useful caution but rejects the controlling move.
4. Respect — Respect the alarm; decline the contract.
rituals.win: ✓ I thanked the alarm for trying to protect me—and declined its contract.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Respect”; keep the compass.
• Shortcut: “Answer M”, once.
• “Answer M” keeps meaning in motion.
• Look back: “Ask Danger” → “Respect”.
• I can use “Thank Intention” while pain stays real.
rituals.formula_flow: Ask Danger → Thank Intention → Answer M → Respect
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not dismiss warnings that point to concrete and immediate danger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THOUGHT DEPARTURES
rituals.goal: Give thought transport, not a throne.
rituals.steps:
1. Place Thought — Place the thought on something already moving: a bus passing, a leaf in drainage water, subtitles leaving a screen.
2. Watch Arrival — Watch its full arrival and departure without pushing it faster.
3. Return Eyes — When the carrier exits, return your eyes to one stationary object.
4. Allow Departure — Another vehicle may come; none owns the station.
rituals.win: ✓ Let the thought pass without giving it the station.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Allow Departure”; loosen the label.
• Restart detected: “Return Eyes”.
• “Return Eyes” — the rule loosened.
• “Place Thought” versus “Allow Departure”: what eased?
• I can use “Watch Arrival” without becoming the label.
rituals.formula_flow: Place Thought → Watch Arrival → Return Eyes → Allow Departure
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop imagery if it increases detachment from surroundings.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: NAME THE SERIES
rituals.goal: This episode has aired before.
rituals.steps:
1. Ignore — Ignore today’s plot for ten seconds.
2. Ask Recurring — Ask what recurring series it belongs to: ‘The Rejection prediction,’ ‘Everyone Is Ahead,’ ‘I Must Fix It Now.’ Give the series a short title and season number.
3. Ask Whether — Then check if this episode contains new information or recycled footage.
rituals.win: ✓ Someone else’s position stopped defining mine.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Ask Whether”; drop the scoreboard.
• Use “Ask Recurring” on return.
• “Ask Recurring” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• Before/after: “Ignore” → “Ask Whether”.
• I can use “Ask Recurring” without ranking my worth.
rituals.formula_flow: Ignore → Ask Recurring → Ask Whether
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Retire any title that ridicules genuine pain or identity.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: COMMAND DOWNGRADE
rituals.goal: Turn the order into a weather report.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture Command — Hear the command exactly as it arrives: ‘Leave now,’ ‘Check again,’ ‘You must reply.’
2. Downgrade It — Remove the command tone and turn it into an observation: ‘An urge to leave is here,’ ‘An urge to check is here,’ or ‘An urge to reply is here.’
3. Reject Authority — Let the urge give you information without giving it authority.
rituals.win: ✓ Wanting became a signal instead of an instruction.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Reject Authority”; let wanting crest.
• Return once to “Downgrade It”.
• “Downgrade It” keeps wanting off controls.
• What lost power: “Picture Command” → “Reject Authority”?
• I can use “Downgrade It” without obeying the urge.
rituals.formula_flow: Picture Command → Reject Authority
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Act immediately when the original command reflects genuine safety needs.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: PASSENGER THOUGHT
rituals.goal: You do not need an empty vehicle to steer.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Time — Choose one two-minute action that matters.
2. Ride Passenger — Invite the thought to ride in the passenger seat—audible, uncomfortable, unedited.
3. Keep Hands — Hold hands on the action wheel and complete the movement while it talks.
4. Who Drove? — At the destination, notice who actually drove.
rituals.win: ✓ Thought stayed in the passenger seat. Steering remained mine.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Who Drove?”; slow the clock.
• Shortcut: “Keep Hands”, once.
• “Keep Hands” puts facts above speed.
• “Who Drove?”: what changed from “Choose Time”?
• I can use “Ride Passenger” without rushing.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Time → Ride Passenger → Keep Hands → Who Drove?
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Shorten the trip if functioning or situational awareness drops.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: MAKE A WIDER CONTAINER
rituals.goal: Capacity grows sideways, not through force.
rituals.steps:
1. Locate Unwanted — Locate the unwanted sensation.
2. Find Edges — Find its edges.
3. Soften Muscles — Soften the muscles around—not inside—it.
4. Include Neutral — Include one neutral body area and one external sound in awareness.
5. Widen the Room — You are enlarging the room, not evicting the guest.
rituals.win: ✓ Made more room around the feeling instead of trying to evict it.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Widen the Room”; keep the compass.
• Loop back? Use “Soften Muscles”.
• “Include Neutral” keeps meaning in motion.
• Before/after: “Locate Unwanted” → “Widen the Room”.
• I can use “Find Edges” while pain stays real.
rituals.formula_flow: Locate Unwanted → Find Edges → Soften Muscles → Include Neutral → Widen the Room
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop and orient outward if expansion produces flooding or feeling unreal or disconnected.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: PAIN PLUS THE FIGHT
rituals.goal: Separate the wound from the fist wrapped around it.
rituals.steps:
1. Make Two Lanes — Imagine two lanes: WHAT HURTS and WHAT RESISTANCE ADDS.
2. Keep The Hurt — In the first lane, picture the raw sensation or fact.
3. Catch The Fight — In the second lane, name demands, self-attack, bracing, and impossible arguments with reality.
4. Drop One Fight — Release one item from the resistance lane while respecting the hurt.
rituals.win: ✓ Hurt stayed respected while one layer of fighting came off.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Drop One Fight”; release extra blame.
• Shortcut: “Catch The Fight”, once.
• “Catch The Fight” keeps blame in proportion.
• Look back: “Make Two Lanes” → “Drop One Fight”.
• I can use “Keep The Hurt” without owning everything.
rituals.formula_flow: Make Two Lanes → Keep The Hurt → Catch The Fight → Drop One Fight
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not use acceptance language to tolerate abuse, injustice, or untreated symptoms.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: CAMERA FIRST, CAPTION SECOND
rituals.goal: Experience arrives before the commentary team.
rituals.steps:
1. Camera Mode — For fifteen seconds, collect camera data: colour, movement, sound, pressure, position.
2. Describe Event — Then say the event using only that footage.
3. Add Caption — Now add the meaning separately and label it CAPTION.
4. Keep Sources — Keep both; never confuse their sources.
rituals.win: ✓ Camera and caption separated. Neither gets to impersonate the other.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Keep Sources”; leave the forecast.
• Use “Add Caption” on return.
• “Add Caption” — fear isn’t fate.
• “Camera Mode” to “Keep Sources”: what loosened?
• I can use “Describe Event” while fear stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Camera Mode → Describe Event → Add Caption → Keep Sources
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Switch to safety action when the facts themselves show immediate risk.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: ENTER THE ACTION
rituals.goal: Stop watching yourself do the thing; do the thing.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Ordinary — Choose one ordinary activity.
2. Place Vision — Place vision, touch, posture, and hearing inside it.
3. Leave Re — When attention leaves, re-enter through the next physical contact point rather than scolding yourself.
4. Stay Activity — Stay until the activity reaches its natural edge.
5. Enter Fully — Participation, not perfect focus, is the target.
rituals.win: ✓ Action got there before perfect focus.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Enter Fully”; release the score.
• On return: “Leave Re”.
• “Stay Activity” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• Look back: “Choose Ordinary” → “Enter Fully”.
• I can use “Place Vision” without perfecting.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Ordinary → Place Vision → Leave Re → Stay Activity → Enter Fully
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not narrow attention during driving, caregiving, or tasks requiring broad awareness.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE ATTENTION BOUNCER
rituals.goal: Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
rituals.steps:
1. Spot Arrival — Notice the next thought without following it.
2. Stamp Access — Stamp it REQUESTED, RELEVANT, or UNINVITED.
3. Set Budget — Give only the chosen category a short timer; let the others wait without argument.
4. Return Door — When the timer ends, return to the task or deliberately admit one new thought.
rituals.win: ✓ The mental pile-up has a front edge again.
rituals.supports:
• One exhale after “Return Door”; redirect attention.
• On return: “Set Budget”.
• “Set Budget” proves one signal leads.
• Difference check: “Spot Arrival” → “Return Door”.
• I can use “Stamp Access” amid noise.
rituals.formula_flow: Spot Arrival → Stamp Access → Set Budget → Return Door
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop if the labels become a checking ritual or make urgent action harder.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: EMOTION, COMPLETE YOUR ARC
rituals.goal: Feelings move differently when they are not put on trial.
rituals.steps:
1. Locate Emotion — Locate the emotion in the body and give it a precise name.
2. Permit — Permit its current intensity without feeding the story.
3. Track Sensation — Track where sensation travels, peaks, breaks, or cools.
4. Follow Appears — Follow until one natural shift appears, then choose the action the situation—not the wave—requires.
rituals.win: ✓ The wave moved through; the situation was still there to choose from.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Follow Appears”; no forcing.
• Shortcut: “Track Sensation”, once.
• “Track Sensation” keeps sensation as data.
• Look back: “Locate Emotion” → “Follow Appears”.
• I can use “Permit” while sensation stays.
rituals.formula_flow: Locate Emotion → Permit → Track Sensation → Follow Appears
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Seek help for escalating self-harm, aggression, panic, or inability to function.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: ONE CLEAN WISH
rituals.goal: Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.
rituals.steps:
1. Bring Person — Bring the person to mind at a safe distance.
2. Keep It Honest — Choose one honest wish that does not deny harm: ‘May we both be free from causing more suffering,’ or ‘May safety become possible.’ Offer it once.
3. State Boundary — Then state the boundary or action you still need.
4. Keep Discernment — Warmth does not cancel discernment.
rituals.win: ✓ Warmth stayed intact without making discernment disappear.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Keep Discernment”; release extra load.
• Return once to “State Boundary”.
• “State Boundary” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• “Bring Person” to “Keep Discernment”: what loosened?
• I can use “Keep It Honest” without carrying it all.
rituals.formula_flow: Bring Person → Keep It Honest → State Boundary → Keep Discernment
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not direct compassion exercises toward an abuser if it weakens necessary distance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE 2% SOFTENING
rituals.goal: Your face can send the body a quieter memo.
rituals.steps:
1. Release Forehead — Without forcing happiness, release the forehead, loosen the eyes, and lift the mouth corners by only two percent.
2. Keep Expression — Keep the expression believable.
3. Hold Neutral — Hold it while looking at one neutral object.
4. Ask Whether — Ask whether defence changed by even half a notch.
rituals.win: ✓ Half a notch was enough to prove defence can soften.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Ask Whether”; no breath-holding.
• Use “Hold Neutral” on return.
• “Hold Neutral” — alarm isn’t command.
• At “Ask Whether”, compare “Release Forehead”.
• I can use “Keep Expression” while alarm rises.
rituals.formula_flow: Release Forehead → Keep Expression → Hold Neutral → Ask Whether
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Skip this if smiling feels unsafe, invalidating, painful, or socially risky.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
rituals.goal: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.
rituals.steps:
1. Set Code — Choose three tiny comfortable movements, such as tap a knee, touch a thumb, and look at one fixed object. Say the order once.
2. Run Order — do A–B–C slowly, pausing after each movement long enough to feel it finish.
3. Reverse Code — do C–B–A at the same pace. If you lose the order, return to neutral and restart instead of speeding up.
4. Claim Control — Name the movement you directed most clearly, then let the whole code stop.
rituals.win: ✓ The body surge lost some of its authority.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Claim Control”; no breath-holding.
• Return once to “Reverse Code”.
• “Reverse Code” — alarm isn’t command.
• At “Claim Control”, compare “Set Code”.
• I can use “Run Order” while alarm rises.
rituals.formula_flow: Set Code → Run Order → Reverse Code → Claim Control
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not play while driving, moving through hazards, dizzy, injured, or unable to stay oriented.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE FOUR-LETTER BRAKE
rituals.goal: Crisis speed must pass four gates before action.
rituals.steps:
1. Stop Nonessential — S — stop every nonessential movement.
2. Take Physical — T — take one physical step back.
3. Observe Facts — O — observe facts, sensations, and the strongest impulse.
4. Proceed Safely — P — proceed with the smallest safe move that will still make sense in an hour.
5. Skip Negotiation — Do not negotiate with momentum between letters.
rituals.win: ✓ Four letters bought enough time to interrupt momentum.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Skip Negotiation”; let wanting crest.
• Loop back? Use “Observe Facts”.
• “Proceed Safely” keeps wanting off controls.
• Before/after: “Stop Nonessential” → “Skip Negotiation”.
• I can use “Take Physical” without obeying the urge.
rituals.formula_flow: Stop Nonessential → Take Physical → Observe Facts → Proceed Safely → Skip Negotiation
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use emergency support when immediate danger cannot be managed by a pause.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: ONE FOOT HERE, ONE FOOT NEAR IT
rituals.goal: Hold distress and safety in the same frame.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Stable — Choose a stable anchor such as feet on the floor or a fixed sound.
2. Keep Most — Keep most attention there while allowing a small edge of distress into awareness.
3. Anchor Verify — Verify the anchor remains present.
4. Tune the Ratio — Adjust the ratio until both can coexist without losing choice.
rituals.win: ✓ The memory moved one step back toward then.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Tune the Ratio”; orient to now.
• Shortcut: “Anchor Verify”, once.
• “Anchor Verify” moves memory toward then.
• “Choose Stable” to “Tune the Ratio”: what loosened?
• I can use “Keep Most” while staying in now.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Stable → Keep Most → Anchor Verify → Tune the Ratio
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Increase anchoring or stop if distress takes the whole field.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: EXHALE IN CHAPTERS
rituals.goal: A large release can become several manageable ones.
rituals.steps:
1. Let Air — Instead of one continuous out-breath, let air leave in three soft portions with tiny unforced spaces between.
2. Keep Face — Keep the face loose and never push to empty.
3. Wait Body — After the final segment, wait for the body’s next inhale rather than grabbing it.
rituals.win: ✓ The narrative stopped owning every room.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Wait Body”; then keep moving.
• If it flares, choose “Keep Face”.
• “Keep Face” proves motion is available.
• Difference check: “Let Air” → “Wait Body”.
• I can use “Keep Face” before motivation.
rituals.formula_flow: Let Air → Keep Face → Wait Body
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Resume normal breathing if segmentation causes urgency or tingling.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: LET THE FIELD SELF-PUBLISH
rituals.goal: Observe experience without appointing a headline.
rituals.steps:
1. Open Field — Open Field with sight, sound, sensation, and thought available at once.
2. Whatever — Notice whatever becomes prominent, then what replaces it.
3. Let All Arrive — Do not select, rank, or hold any item.
4. Track the Shift — Track the changing editorial order for one minute.
rituals.win: ✓ A belief moved from law to hypothesis.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Track the Shift”; loosen the label.
• Use “Let All Arrive” on return.
• “Let All Arrive” — the rule loosened.
• Difference check: “Open Field” → “Track the Shift”.
• I can use “Whatever” without becoming the label.
rituals.formula_flow: Open Field → Whatever → Let All Arrive → Track the Shift
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Open monitoring should stop if unstructured awareness feels overwhelming.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: NO FAVOURITE SENSATION
rituals.goal: Receive what arrives without keeping or ejecting it.
rituals.steps:
1. Let Field — Let the field choose its next foreground.
2. Pleasant — Pleasant, unpleasant, dull, or vivid—offer each the same brief hospitality.
3. Include Movement — When preference reaches to grip or reject, include that movement too.
4. End Whole — End by noticing the whole room at once.
rituals.win: ✓ A physical signal lost its automatic meaning.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “End Whole”; leave the forecast.
• Shortcut: “Include Movement”, once.
• “Include Movement” — fear isn’t fate.
• Look back: “Let Field” → “End Whole”.
• I can use “Pleasant” while fear stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Let Field → Pleasant → Include Movement → End Whole
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use a stable anchor instead during high body alarm or feeling unreal or disconnected.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE SENSE ROLL CALL
rituals.goal: Make the present answer in specifics.
rituals.steps:
1. Find Five — Find five distinct colours or shapes, four contact sensations, three separate sounds, two scents, and one taste or mouth sensation.
2. Answer Blue — No generic answers; ‘blue attention’ beats ‘something blue.’ Let the inventory end with the most stable item.
rituals.win: ✓ Five senses checked in; one steady detail got the last word.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Answer Blue”; notice the room.
• Skip replay; use “Answer Blue”.
• “Find Five” proves the present returned.
• “Find Five” to “Answer Blue”: what loosened?
• I can use “Answer Blue” to return here.
rituals.formula_flow: Find Five → Answer Blue
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Adapt counts or omit channels that are unavailable or triggering.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: EXPAND–GATHER–EXPAND
rituals.goal: Move awareness through an hourglass.
rituals.steps:
1. Acknowledge — First, acknowledge the full weather of the moment.
2. Breathe Small — Next, gather attention around breathing as a small centre.
3. Widen Whole — Finally, widen to the whole body and surrounding space.
4. Spend — Spend roughly one minute in each shape.
5. Carry Final — Carry the final wide frame into your next movement.
rituals.win: ✓ There is space between the mind and what it produced.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Carry Final”; no forcing.
• If it flares, choose “Widen Whole”.
• “Spend” keeps sensation as data.
• What changed: “Acknowledge” → “Carry Final”?
• I can use “Breathe Small” while sensation stays.
rituals.formula_flow: Acknowledge → Breathe Small → Widen Whole → Spend → Carry Final
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use a non-breath anchor if respiration is activating.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: RAIN WITHOUT THE UMBRELLA
rituals.goal: Meet the experience before trying to change the prediction.
rituals.steps:
1. Recognise — Recognise what is here.
2. Allow Moment — Allow this moment of it to exist.
3. Question About — Investigate with one kind question about body or need.
4. Experience — Notice that the experience is present but not the whole of you.
5. Move R — Move through R–A–I–N once; resolution is not a required fifth letter.
rituals.win: ✓ The experience was met without making resolution a requirement.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Move R”; no forcing.
• Skip replay; use “Question About”.
• “Experience” keeps sensation as data.
• Keep one lesson: “Recognise” → “Move R”.
• I can use “Allow Moment” while sensation stays.
rituals.formula_flow: Recognise → Allow Moment → Question About → Experience → Move R
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Skip investigation when acute distress requires stabilisation first.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: FOUR PARTS OF ONE STEP
rituals.goal: Walking can become a moving attention track.
rituals.steps:
1. Place Weight — Slow enough to separate lift, travel, place, and weight transfer.
2. Follow Events — Follow those four events through several steps.
3. Thought — When thought pulls away, rejoin at whichever phase the foot is currently performing.
4. Finish Walking — Finish by walking normally while retaining one point of contact.
rituals.win: ✓ Walking stayed ordinary while attention stayed connected.
rituals.supports:
• One exhale after “Finish Walking”; redirect attention.
• Skip replay; use “Thought”.
• “Thought” proves one signal leads.
• “Place Weight” to “Finish Walking”: what loosened?
• I can use “Follow Events” amid noise.
rituals.formula_flow: Place Weight → Follow Events → Thought → Finish Walking
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Practise only where slowed walking is physically safe.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: LISTEN PAST THE SOUND
rituals.goal: The disappearance is part of the Notice.
rituals.steps:
1. Play Safe — Ring, play, or notice a safe sustained sound.
2. Follow Decay — Follow its decay with precision until you cannot locate any remainder.
3. Stay Silence — Stay with the silence that receives it, not with memory of the tone.
4. Let Surroundings — Let the next surroundings sound end the practice.
rituals.win: ✓ The sound stopped owning the whole moment.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Let Surroundings”; leave the forecast.
• If it flares, choose “Stay Silence”.
• “Stay Silence” — fear isn’t fate.
• Look back: “Play Safe” → “Let Surroundings”.
• I can use “Follow Decay” while fear stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Play Safe → Follow Decay → Stay Silence → Let Surroundings
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Avoid intense volume or tones associated with distress.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: NOTICE THE NOTICING
rituals.goal: Turn attention toward the fact that experience is known.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Sensation — Choose any sensation.
2. Recognise — First recognise its qualities.
3. Ask Verbally — Then ask, without answering verbally, ‘How is this already known?’ Rest with the immediacy of knowing rather than searching for an object called awareness.
4. Return Fact — Return by naming one visible fact.
rituals.win: ✓ Awareness noticed itself—then landed back on one visible fact.
rituals.supports:
• One exhale after “Return Fact”; redirect attention.
• Shortcut: “Ask Verbally”, once.
• “Ask Verbally” proves one signal leads.
• At “Return Fact”, compare “Choose Sensation”.
• I can use “Recognise” amid noise.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Sensation → Recognise → Ask Verbally → Return Fact
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Discontinue if self-referential attention increases unreality.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE BREATH HINGE
rituals.goal: Rest where one phase becomes another.
rituals.steps:
1. Follow Inhale — Follow a natural inhale to the instant it turns toward exhale.
2. Leave Hinge Free — Do not hold or stretch the hinge.
3. Change — Notice the same effortless change at the bottom of exhalation.
4. Allow Breaths — Visit each threshold lightly, then allow several breaths to pass unwatched.
rituals.win: ✓ Starting became smaller than the story around starting.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Allow Breaths”; then keep moving.
• Use “Change” on return.
• “Change” proves motion is available.
• What lost power: “Follow Inhale” → “Allow Breaths”?
• I can use “Leave Hinge Free” before motivation.

rituals.title: WHERE SOUND BECOMES HEARING
rituals.goal: Trace vibration to its inner arrival point.
rituals.steps:
1. Listen Sustained — Listen to a sustained, gentle sound.
2. Follow Apparent — Follow it from apparent distance toward the place where it becomes an auditory experience—ear, head, body, or nowhere locatable.
3. Rest Briefly — When the border between outside vibration and inside hearing blurs, rest there briefly.

rituals.supports:

rituals.safety:

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: BORROW THE SKY’S WIDTH
rituals.goal: Let vision teach attention another size.
rituals.steps:
1. Open Sky — Gaze softly into open sky or another unobstructed safe field.
2. Release Pinpoint — Release pinpoint focus and include the edges of vision.
3. Compare Width — Without forcing calm, compare the width outside with the contraction inside.
4. Keep Wide View — Allow attention to occupy both.
rituals.win: ✓ The view widened enough for thought and sky to coexist.

• One exhale after “Keep Wide View”; redirect attention.
• Shortcut: “Compare Width”, once.
• “Compare Width” proves one signal leads.
• “Open Sky” to “Keep Wide View”: what loosened?

rituals.safety:

Never sky-gaze while driving or in unsafe light and weather.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE BODY AS INNER SPACE
rituals.goal: Trade the sense of a solid block for a more spacious inner map.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine Torso — Imagine the torso and limbs as volumes containing room rather than dense objects.
2. Cavities — Notice cavities, distances, and open intervals inside the body inner picture while maintaining feet, seat, and external orientation in space.
3. Keep Image — Keep the image gentle and anatomically nonliteral.
rituals.win: ✓ The body image became more spacious without needing to become literal.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Keep Image”; notice the room.
• Return once to “Cavities”.
• “Cavities” proves the present returned.
• Compare “Imagine Torso” with “Keep Image”.
• I can use “Cavities” to return here.
rituals.formula_flow: Imagine Torso → Cavities → Keep Image
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop immediately if the exercise makes you feel unreal, disconnected, numb, or less oriented to the room.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: CATCH WANTING BEFORE THE OBJECT
rituals.goal: Desire starts moving before it names a destination.
rituals.steps:
1. Wait Pull — Wait at the first pull: leaning, brightening, reaching, mental zoom.
2. Observe Wanting — For five seconds, observe wanting as raw movement without completing ‘I want…’.
3. Name Object — Only afterward name the object and decide whether pursuit serves the wider situation.
rituals.win: ✓ Wanting and doing are separate again.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Name Object”; leave the forecast.
• Use “Observe Wanting” on return.
• “Observe Wanting” — fear isn’t fate.
• “Wait Pull” to “Name Object”: what loosened?
• I can use “Observe Wanting” while fear stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Wait Pull → Observe Wanting → Name Object
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use added support for dangerous cravings or impaired control.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: WATCH PLEASURE LEAVE CLEANLY
rituals.goal: The ending of pleasantness is not a failure.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Mild — Choose a mild enjoyable sensation.
2. Track Rise — Track its rise, fullness, thinning, and the eventual return to neutral.
3. Resist — Resist grabbing for a second dose during the fading phase.
4. Let Pleasure Leave — Notice what remains when the pleasant signal is gone.
rituals.win: ✓ Pleasure ended cleanly without turning the ending into a problem.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Let Pleasure Leave”; leave the forecast.
• On return: “Resist”.
• “Resist” — fear isn’t fate.
• “Choose Mild” to “Let Pleasure Leave”: what loosened?
• I can use “Track Rise” while fear stays loud.

rituals.safety:

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: NOT FOR, NOT AGAINST
rituals.goal: Release both hands of mental grasping.
rituals.steps:
1. Check The Pull — Notice whether experience is being pulled closer or pushed away.
2. Relax — Relax the corresponding inner movement without demanding neutrality.
3. Let Content — Let the content remain unowned and unobstructed for a short interval.
4. Act According — Then act according to circumstance, not attraction or aversion.
rituals.win: ✓ Rejection became an event, not an identity.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Act According”; drop the scoreboard.
• Catch restart with “Let Content”.
• “Let Content” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• “Act According”: what changed from “Check The Pull”?
• I can use “Relax” without ranking my worth.

rituals.safety:

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: STAY AT THE SENSE DOOR
rituals.goal: What you notice can occur without being kidnapped by the object.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Sound — Choose one sound or sight.
2. Sensory — Notice the first sensory contact, then keep attention at the doorway of hearing or seeing rather than following associations outward.
3. Return Bare — When the mind travels to the object’s story, return to bare contact.
rituals.win: ✓ Story dropped away; bare sensation was enough.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Return Bare”; notice the room.
• Restart detected: “Sensory”.
• “Sensory” proves the present returned.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: WHO RECEIVED THAT THOUGHT?
rituals.goal: Turn inquiry toward the assumed owner.
rituals.steps:
1. Ask Whom — When a thought appears, ask ‘To whom did this occur?’ If ‘me’ arises, ask ‘What is this me before the answer?’ Refuse biography, role, body description, and philosophy.
2. Hold Question — Stay with the question’s open edge for several heartbeats.
rituals.win: ✓ The label stayed readable without staying absolute.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Hold Question”; loosen the label.
• Loop back? Use “Hold Question”.
• “Ask Whom” — the rule loosened.
• At “Hold Question”, compare “Ask Whom”.
• I can use “Hold Question” without becoming the label.

rituals.safety:

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: REMOVE THE NAME BADGES
rituals.goal: See what remains when roles clock out briefly.
rituals.steps:
1. Name — Name the roles active today. Keep the pace deliberately slow here.
2. Imagine Badge — One by one, imagine placing each badge on a table—parent, worker, partner, achiever, patient, helper.
3. Release Roles — Sit without using any badge to answer ‘Who am I now?’ After a short pause, reclaim only the role needed next.
rituals.win: ✓ I took the name badges off and noticed I was still here.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Release Roles”; leave the forecast.
• Pulled back? Touch “Imagine Badge”.
• “Imagine Badge” — fear isn’t fate.
• Keep one lesson: “Name” → “Release Roles”.
• I can use “Imagine Badge” while fear stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Name → Imagine Badge → Release Roles
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep grounding and avoid role stripping if identity feels fragile.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER
rituals.goal: Feelings that seem tangled may be answering different moments.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Mix — Name up to three present feelings. Do not explain them yet.
2. Find First — Which arrived first? Put it at the left of a short line.
3. Link Cue — Add the concrete cue that each feeling answered—words heard, an image, a body change, or a later thought.
4. Read Order — Read the sequence once: ‘First ___ answered ___; then ___ answered ___.’ Stop after the order is clear.
rituals.win: ✓ The tangle became a sequence. Each feeling got its own moment.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Read Order”; let wanting crest.
• Restart detected: “Link Cue”.
• “Link Cue” keeps wanting off controls.
• “Name Mix” → “Read Order”: what changed?
• I can use “Find First” without obeying the urge.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Mix → Find First → Link Cue → Read Order
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop if sequencing pulls you into flashback, self-blame, numbness, or forced certainty about the past.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE THREE QUALITIES WEATHER REPORT
rituals.goal: Mental states are climates, not surnames.
rituals.steps:
1. Classify — Sort the current movement as clarity, agitation, inertia, or a mixture.
2. Speed — Notice its speed, energy, and attentional style.
3. Choose Smallest — Choose the smallest balancing condition—rest for agitation, body alarm for inertia, protection for clarity.
4. Say Recheck — Recheck later without saying ‘I am this.’
rituals.win: ✓ I read the inner weather without turning it into an identity.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Say Recheck”; then keep moving.
• Return once to “Choose Smallest”.
• “Choose Smallest” proves motion is available.
• “Classify” versus “Say Recheck”: what eased?
• I can use “Speed” before motivation.
rituals.formula_flow: Classify → Speed → Choose Smallest → Say Recheck
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE SIX-LINK FIRE CHAIN
rituals.goal: Anger often begins several stations before the explosion.
rituals.steps:
1. Trace Sequence — Trace the sequence backward: confusion or loss of judgement; anger; frustrated desire; attachment; repeated attention; original cue.
2. Earliest — Find the earliest link still reachable now. Use the simplest true sentence you can.
3. Remove Fuel — Remove fuel there—shift attention, loosen attachment, or revise the demand.
rituals.win: ✓ I found one link feeding the fire and removed fuel there.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Remove Fuel”; soften the jaw.
• Catch restart with “Earliest”.
• “Earliest” keeps clarity above heat.
• Keep one lesson: “Trace Sequence” → “Remove Fuel”.
• I can use “Earliest” without extra heat.
rituals.formula_flow: Trace Sequence → Earliest → Remove Fuel
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Create distance; obtain help whenever aggression or violence risk is present.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT
rituals.goal: Silence often disappears because the mind fills it immediately.
rituals.steps:
1. Wait Thought — Wait for a thought to end naturally.
2. Empty — At the first empty beat, resist generating commentary about emptiness.
3. Rest Duration — Rest for the duration available—even a fraction.
4. Let Thought — Let the next thought arise without invitation.
5. Count Gap — Count the gap only after it is over.
rituals.win: ✓ What matters stayed reachable inside the loss.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Count Gap”; keep the compass.
• Pulled back? Touch “Rest Duration”.
• “Let Thought” keeps meaning in motion.
• What changed: “Wait Thought” → “Count Gap”?
• I can use “Empty” while pain stays real.
rituals.formula_flow: Wait Thought → Empty → Rest Duration → Let Thought → Count Gap
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use external engagement if silence feels frightening or destabilising.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: PAY FOR THE NEXT LAP
rituals.goal: Another lap costs minutes of your actual life.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Lap — Name the exact question you want one more thinking lap to answer. One sentence only.
2. Price Trade — Choose what those three minutes will replace: rest, a message, food, movement, work, or a decision. Say the trade plainly.
3. Buy Three — If the trade is worth it, set three minutes and think only about the named question. If not, close the lap now.
4. Close Toll — When the clock ends, stop without buying another lap. Do the displaced activity or deliberately let it go.
rituals.win: ✓ Toll paid once. No second lap purchased.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Close Toll”; end the lap.
• Skip replay; use “Buy Three”.
• “Buy Three” proves loops can stop.
• At “Close Toll”, compare “Name Lap”.
• I can use “Price Trade” without another lap.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Lap → Price Trade → Buy Three → Close Toll
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Never buy another analysis lap with sleep, medication, food, immediate safety, or time-critical responsibilities.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: IMAGINE THE FEELING’S SHAPE
rituals.goal: Visual form can hold what words flatten.
rituals.steps:
1. Assign Colour — Without aiming for beauty, assign the state a colour, texture, shape, size, and position in your mind.
2. Add Boundary — Add a boundary, pressure source, and possible exit route.
3. Change One Feature — Change one visual property and notice whether the inner state shifts.
rituals.win: ✓ I changed the feeling’s shape and watched the inner state answer back.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Change One Feature”; release extra load.

• “Add Boundary” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• Before/after: “Assign Colour” → “Change One Feature”.
• I can use “Add Boundary” without carrying it all.
rituals.formula_flow: Assign Colour → Add Boundary → Change One Feature
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop if imagery becomes graphic, compulsive, or more disturbing.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: PUT THE MEMORY BACK IN PAST TENSE
rituals.goal: Grammar can accidentally keep history live.
rituals.steps:
1. Use Happened — Retell one short segment using was, happened, had, and then.
2. Ground Between — After every emotionally loaded sentence, insert three present facts: your present location, the current year, and what choice exists now.
3. Finish Moment — Finish with: ‘That ended; this moment is different.’
rituals.win: ✓ The sentence moved the memory back into past tense.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Finish Moment”; let feeling settle.
• Return once to “Ground Between”.
• “Ground Between” separates feeling from fact.
• “Finish Moment”: what changed from “Use Happened”?
• I can use “Ground Between” while emotion stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Use Happened → Ground Between → Finish Moment
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not retell alone if the memory overwhelms sense of where you are.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THREE SELVES, THREE JOBS
rituals.goal: Present-you should not do every time period’s labour.
rituals.steps:
1. Make Time Zones — Picture three time zones: PAST, PRESENT, FUTURE.
2. Complete Actions — Place completed actions in PAST, available repair in PRESENT, and prevention plans in FUTURE.
3. Reassign — Move any item that belongs to the wrong time zone.
4. Do Present Job — do only one PRESENT task now.
rituals.win: ✓ Present-me did present-me’s job and stopped carrying the other two shifts.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Do Present Job”; end the lap.
• Pulled back? Touch “Reassign”.
• “Reassign” proves loops can stop.
• At “Do Present Job”, compare “Make Time Zones”.
• I can use “Complete Actions” without another lap.
rituals.formula_flow: Make Time Zones → Complete Actions → Reassign → Do Present Job
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not use time ownership to evade current accountability for earlier harm.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: PUT THE YEARS BACK BETWEEN THEM
rituals.goal: Put the real years back between then and now.
rituals.steps:
1. Date Events — Picture the dates of the events that currently feel piled together.
2. Scale Distance — Give equal physical space to equal spans of time; do not place every event in one crowded cluster.
3. Present — Notice TODAY at the correct distance and name one fact that belongs only to now.
4. Recheck Urgency — Look again at the oldest event and rate how immediate it feels after the spacing is restored.
rituals.win: ✓ Speed stopped masquerading as necessity.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Recheck Urgency”; slow the clock.
• If it flares, choose “Present”.
• “Present” puts facts above speed.
• What lost power: “Date Events” → “Recheck Urgency”?
• I can use “Scale Distance” without rushing.
rituals.formula_flow: Date Events → Scale Distance → Present → Recheck Urgency
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop and reorient to the room if the timeline makes the past feel more present.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: DELETE ‘AM’ FROM THE SENTENCE
rituals.goal: Identity verbs can turn weather into a prison.
rituals.steps:
1. Drop Identity Verb — Restate ‘I am broken/lazy/anxious’ without am or is.
2. Use Temporary — Use temporary action language: ‘Avoiding has increased this week,’ ‘Anxiety is moving through the chest,’ ‘Energy dropped after…’.
3. Add Condition — Add one condition under which the process changes.
rituals.win: ✓ The emotion became evidence to consider, not evidence that decides.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Add Condition”; let feeling settle.
• Return once to “Use Temporary”.
• “Use Temporary” separates feeling from fact.
• “Drop Identity Verb” → “Add Condition”: what changed?
• I can use “Use Temporary” while emotion stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Drop Identity Verb → Use Temporary → Add Condition
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep diagnostic terms where clinically useful; remove only overgeneralised identity.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THIRD-PERSON OWNERSHIP TEST
rituals.goal: Grammar can loosen the grip without denying the experience.
rituals.steps:
1. Describe Event — Frame the moment once as ‘this mind is predicting…’ or ‘the system is producing…’.
2. Change — Notice what changes in intensity, responsibility, and choice.
3. Return Person — Then return to first person for the action you really own: ‘I will…’.
4. Loosen the Grammar — Distance the content, not agency.
rituals.win: ✓ I loosened the grammar without giving away ownership of the experience.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Loosen the Grammar”; end the lap.
• Skip replay; use “Return Person”.
• “Return Person” proves loops can stop.
• Before/after: “Describe Event” → “Loosen the Grammar”.
• I can use “Change” without another lap.
rituals.formula_flow: Describe Event → Change → Return Person → Loosen the Grammar
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop if altered pronouns increase estrangement from self.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: ZOOM LENS TRAINING
rituals.goal: Attention needs more than one focal length.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Object — Select an object.
2. Spend — Spend ten seconds on one tiny feature, ten on the object and nearby context, and ten on the whole visual field.
3. Repeat Shift — Repeat in reverse.
4. Select Aperture — Select the aperture that best fits the actual task.
rituals.win: ✓ I changed focal length instead of forcing one kind of attention to do every job.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Select Aperture”; keep both sides.

• “Repeat Shift” widens the evidence field.
• “Select Aperture”: what changed from “Choose Object”?

rituals.formula_flow: Choose Object → Spend → Repeat Shift → Select Aperture
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use broad awareness in environments that require hazard monitoring.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE PRICE OF KEEPING THIS SELF
rituals.goal: Every identity grants permissions and charges fees.
rituals.steps:
1. Sort Identity Costs — Imagine three buckets: IT LETS ME; IT STOPS ME; IT DEMANDS FROM ME.
2. Fill The Buckets — Mentally sort the self-concept into those three buckets.
3. Find The Price — Focus on the highest hidden cost and ask whether the identity still earns its keep.
rituals.win: ✓ Thought stopped earning time simply by returning.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Find The Price”; end the lap.
• On return, repeat “Fill The Buckets”.
• “Fill The Buckets” proves loops can stop.
• Difference check: “Sort Identity Costs” → “Find The Price”.
• I can use “Fill The Buckets” without another lap.
rituals.formula_flow: Sort Identity Costs → Fill The Buckets → Find The Price
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Preserve identities that provide community, protection, or meaning unless change is genuinely chosen.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: CALL THE INNER COUNCIL
rituals.goal: Conflicting parts need coordination, not forced unanimity.
rituals.steps:
1. Give Self — Give each self-state a seat.
2. Sentence — One sentence each: what I need, what I fear, what I propose.
3. Protect Whole — Appoint a chair whose job is to protect the whole system over time.
4. Chair the Council — The chair may combine, delay, or reject proposals, but must acknowledge every need.
rituals.win: ✓ Every inner voice got heard; none got automatic control.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Chair the Council”; end the lap.
• Loop back? Use “Protect Whole”.
• “Protect Whole” proves loops can stop.
• “Give Self” versus “Chair the Council”: what eased?
• I can use “Sentence” without another lap.
rituals.formula_flow: Give Self → Sentence → Protect Whole → Chair the Council
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use professional support if parts feel autonomous, dangerous, or disorganising.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: ADD THE WITNESS WHO SHOULD HAVE BEEN THERE
rituals.goal: The remembered self deserves credible rethought.
rituals.steps:
1. Introduce — Introduce a compassionate observer appropriate to the event—a trusted adult, advocate, elder, clinician, or current-you.
2. Name Wrong — Have them name what was wrong, what protection was deserved, and what is true about the person who endured it.
3. Keep It Believable — Keep their words believable.
rituals.win: ✓ The missing witness finally sounded believable, not magical.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Keep It Believable”; watch the thought.
• Catch restart with “Name Wrong”.
• “Name Wrong” proves thought is observable.
• Compare “Introduce” with “Keep It Believable”.
• I can use “Name Wrong” without obeying thought.
rituals.formula_flow: Introduce → Name Wrong → Keep It Believable
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use guided trauma work if imagined witnessing intensifies grief or flashback.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: RELATIONSHIP DATA, NOT ONE BIG FEELING
rituals.goal: Separate episodes before declaring the pattern.
rituals.steps:
1. Hold Event — For recent interactions, hold event, context, frequency, repair attempt, and outcome as separate mental snapshots. Let your weight settle into the chair or floor.
2. Look Repetition — Look for repetition and exceptions.
3. Issue Narrow — Issue a narrow conclusion tied to the observed period rather than ‘always’ or ‘never.’
rituals.win: ✓ The relationship stopped collapsing into one giant feeling.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Issue Narrow”; keep both sides.
• Shortcut: “Look Repetition”, once.
• “Look Repetition” widens the evidence field.
• Compare “Hold Event” with “Issue Narrow”.
• I can use “Look Repetition” before concluding.
rituals.formula_flow: Hold Event → Look Repetition → Issue Narrow
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not use data collection to remain in an unsafe relationship.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: APOLOGY NEEDS THREE EVIDENCE POINTS
rituals.goal: A real apology leaves evidence, not just a tone.
rituals.steps:
1. Return Define — Define what adequate repair requires: clear acknowledgement, changed action, and prevention of return.
2. Specify — Specify what evidence would show each over time.
3. Evaluate — Check the apology against those criteria rather than immediate emotion.
rituals.win: ✓ The apology had to produce evidence before emotion could approve it.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Evaluate”; let feeling settle.
• Pulled back? Touch “Specify”.
• “Specify” separates feeling from fact.
• What changed: “Return Define” → “Evaluate”?
• I can use “Specify” while emotion stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Return Define → Specify → Evaluate
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
No repair test obliges renewed contact after serious harm.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: SET THE CONTACT DOSE
rituals.goal: Closeness can be realistic instead of accepted or abandoned completely.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Frequency — Before contact, choose frequency, duration, permitted topics, location, and exit phrase.
2. Start Lowest — Start with the lowest dose that preserves both connection and regulation.
3. Use Body — Review afterward using body and behaviour, not guilt.
rituals.win: ✓ I set a dose of contact my body and behaviour can actually review.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Use Body”; keep both sides.
• Return once to “Start Lowest”.
• “Start Lowest” widens the evidence field.
• What lost power: “Choose Frequency” → “Use Body”?
• I can use “Start Lowest” before concluding.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Frequency → Start Lowest → Use Body
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Reduce or end contact when boundaries are ignored or safety is compromised.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: WHAT SPECIES OF UNKNOWN IS THIS?
rituals.goal: Different uncertainties require different responses.
rituals.steps:
1. Classify — Categorise the unknown: answerable now, answerable later, influenceable but unknowable, or permanently unknowable.
2. Apply Move — Apply its matching move—research, schedule, act on influence, or practise acceptance.
3. Use Category — Refuse to use one category’s tool on another.
rituals.win: ✓ The unknown got a species name—and finally received the right tool.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Use Category”; leave it unanswered.
• Loop back? Use “Apply Move”.
• “Apply Move” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• Look back: “Classify” → “Use Category”.
• I can use “Apply Move” without a guarantee.

rituals.title: PLAN BOTH BRANCHES
rituals.goal: Uncertainty need not prevent preparation.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Plausible — Choose two plausible outcomes and build a short branch for each: first signal, first action, resource, and exit.
2. Prepare Both — Prepare any step useful in both branches now.
3. Select Path — Delay preference until evidence selects the path.
rituals.win: ✓ Both futures got a plan before either one earned belief.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Select Path”; leave it unanswered.
• Re-entry move: “Prepare Both”.
• “Prepare Both” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• “Choose Plausible” to “Select Path”: what loosened?
• I can use “Prepare Both” without a guarantee.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Plausible → Prepare Both → Select Path
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Add branches only when they are genuinely plausible and decision-relevant.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
